# Reeds–Shepp reference

`reeds-shepp-ompl.csv` contains 128 `(x, y, yaw, shortest_length)` cases at unit turning radius, generated by independently compiling OMPL's original C++ closed-form implementation with `g++ -O2 -static -static-libgcc -static-libstdc++ -std=c++17`. Static C++ runtime linking avoided a host DLL version conflict. The production implementation is Rust and does not call that executable.

Source: https://github.com/ompl/ompl/blob/main/src/ompl/base/spaces/src/ReedsSheppStateSpace.cpp. The source was reconstructed from all 578 numbered lines returned by the web reader after local TLS transport failed. Its saved SHA-256 was `29e8aac5a6080d9a990107c9cb5d7490511362e7680039f4b87ceeb45bbc9987`. The temporary standalone reference harness lives in `target/parking-reference`; its mathematical functions and path-selection logic are unchanged, with the OMPL type declarations reproduced locally and Boost's pi constant replaced by `std::acos(-1.0)`.

Cases use `x=((i*73)%109-54)/8`, `y=((i*37)%107-53)/9`, and `yaw=sin(i*0.371)*pi` for `i=0..127`. This checks the Rust port against independently executed upstream code, in addition to endpoint, symmetry, scale, cusp and closed-form lower-bound tests. Source attribution and BSD terms are retained in `vendor/licenses/OMPL-ReedsShepp.txt` and included in portable packages.
